text:
maria_ml: Putting this here — brought up atlas40k-q8 on ded fleet for onboarding. We see a deterministic quality cliff and occasional token replay when a long anchor crosses the 48k boundary (exactly around 49152 +/- a few). Artifacts: s3://redwood-qa/triage/1768890123/ (logs, kv_dumps, attn_traces). :warning:

maria_ml: repro I used:
```
./run_infer --model atlas40k-q8 --context 49152 --prompt long_anchor_repeat.txt --seed 7 --max_new_tokens 20000 --shard-cache on --streaming
```

maria_ml: truncated log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-23T02:02:03Z] idx=49140 token="and"
[2026-03-23T02:02:03Z] idx=49141 token="and"
[2026-03-23T02:02:04Z] idx=49142 token="and"
[2026-03-23T02:02:04Z] divergence_at=49142 entropy_delta=+5.9
```

sam_infra: hmm. similar to previous shard alignment issues but the 48k boundary is new. did we change fragment sizing recently? I see a config tweak for fragment_size from 16384 -> 12288 last week on the sharding service.

jules_research: if fragment_size changed, index math for rotary normalization might now rebase at unexpected offsets when fragments are stitched. Quant math (q8) could exacerbate because rounding changes effective rotation.

maria_ml: note: when i force `--shard-cache off` (i.e., single shard, no networked reassembly) the issue disappears. This is definitely about cross-shard stitching.

jules_research: can we get the sequence of fragment ids and their absolute offsets during prefill? sample log line to add:
```
PREFILL_FRAG shard_id=7 offset=40960 seq=3 total=5
```

maria_ml: added that logging and re-ran; uploaded prefill_sequence.log. sample: `PREFILL_FRAG shard_id=0 offset=0 seq=0 total=5; PREFILL_FRAG shard_id=1 offset=12288 seq=1 total=5; PREFILL_FRAG shard_id=3 offset=36864 seq=3 total=5; PREFILL_FRAG shard_id=2 offset=24576 seq=2 total=5` — ordering seq jump present.

tim_oncall: that ordering (0,1,3,2) smells like the async memcpy scheduling bug we patched in rwinfer-1.9.4. I rolled that yesterday morning. cc @sam_infra

sam_infra: i can repro ordering on a canary by toggling the memcpy path. if we reproduce, next step is to verify deserialization asserts and add monotonicity checks. i'll spin a canary with fallback memcpy path now.

nina_eval: from eval metrics: continuity_score goes from 0.92 -> 0.47 at 49k, and hallucination_rate +12ppt. We need a clear A/B for product: float32 baseline vs q8 pre-patch vs q8 post-patch. maria, can you gate those runs?

maria_ml: starting matrix: baseline fp32, q8 w/ rwinfer-1.9.3 (prepatch), q8 w/ rwinfer-1.9.4 (postpatch). collecting: token divergence point, ngram continuity, attn head similarity, kv_key_norms, fragment_sequence logs. Uploads go to s3 path above under /matrix_runs.

prefill-bot: Scheduled job: kv-shard-order-check x50 on pool=ded-canary-1. Estimated runtime ~45m.

jules_research: additional micro-check: dump rotary phase for a sample position before and after stitch. if phases mismatch by ~2*pi*k we get wrap artifact; if mismatch is small but multiplied by many heads it can still cause token drift. script:
```python
p_before = rotary.phase_at(pos=49144)
p_after = rotary.phase_at(pos=49160)
print(p_before, p_after, wrap_diff(p_before,p_after))
```

maria_ml: ran that on q8/postpatch and q8/prepatch. prepatch: wrap_diff ~0.001. postpatch: wrap_diff ~0.63 (radians). dumping per-head delta to attn_deltas.csv.

sam_infra: ok that is a smoking gun. looks like certain fragment orders lead to region written with wrong absolute indices and rotary uses those wrong indices during inference. the memcpy kernel path we changed can reorder fragment completions under contention. will revert the patch on ded fleet until we land an ordered-commit fix.

nina_eval: pls tag me when matrix completes. i'll run the eval harness to produce the A/B report (continuity curve vs token index + human spot-check samples).

maria_ml: note for postmortem: add an invariant check in prefill assembler: assert that the reconstructed absolute offsets monotonic increase. also persist fragment seq numbers in event logs for easier debugging.

prefill-bot: kv-shard-order-check run completed (id=run-1768890123-1): failures=3/50, reproducible when memcopy=fast-path and shard-cache=on.

sam_infra: rolling back rwinfer memcpy fast-path on ded-canary-1. Will monitor for any regressions.

jules_research: follow-up experiments to run: 1) same scenario with int4 quant to see sensitivity, 2) repeat with varying fragment_size to find safe thresholds, 3) add randomized reordering fuzz tests to CI. I'll open a GH issue with testplan.

maria_ml: thank you all. leaving artifacts and a short README in s3. I'll update when nina posts the A/B. :white_check_mark:
